30: function matchRoutes(routeConfig: RouteConfig[], pathname: string) {

32:   // component, but we load route components with string paths.
33:   // We don't actually access component here, so it's fine.
34:   return reactRouterMatchRoutes(routeConfig, pathname);

37: type BrokenLink = {
38:   link: string;
39:   resolvedLink: string;
40:   anchor: boolean;
41: };
42: 
43: type BrokenLinksMap = {[pathname: string]: BrokenLink[]};
44: 
45: // The linking data that has been collected on Docusaurus pages during SSG
46: // {rendered page pathname => links and anchors collected on that page}
47: type CollectedLinks = {
48:   [pathname: string]: {links: string[]; anchors: string[]};
49: };
50: 
51: // We use efficient data structures for performance reasons
52: // See https://github.com/facebook/docusaurus/issues/9754
53: type CollectedLinksNormalized = Map<
54:   string,
55:   {links: Set<string>; anchors: Set<string>}
56: >;
57: 
58: type BrokenLinksHelper = {
59:   collectedLinks: CollectedLinksNormalized;
60:   isPathBrokenLink: (linkPath: URLPath) => boolean;
61:   isAnchorBrokenLink: (linkPath: URLPath) => boolean;
62: };
63: 
64: function createBrokenLinksHelper({
65:   collectedLinks,
66:   routes,
67: }: {
68:   collectedLinks: CollectedLinksNormalized;
69:   routes: RouteConfig[];
70: }): BrokenLinksHelper {
71:   const validPathnames = new Set(collectedLinks.keys());
72: 
73:   // IMPORTANT: this is an optimization
74:   // See https://github.com/facebook/docusaurus/issues/9754
75:   // Matching against the route array can be expensive
76:   // If the route is already in the valid pathnames,
77:   // we can avoid matching against it
78:   const remainingRoutes = (function filterRoutes() {
79:     // Goal: unit tests should behave the same with this enabled or disabled
80:     const disableOptimization = false;
81:     if (disableOptimization) {
82:       return routes;
83:     }
84:     // We must consider the "exact" and "strict" match attribute
85:     // We can only infer pre-validated pathnames from a route from exact routes
86:     const [validPathnameRoutes, otherRoutes] = _.partition(
87:       routes,
88:       (route) => route.exact && validPathnames.has(route.path),
89:     );
90:     // If a route is non-strict (non-sensitive to trailing slashes)
91:     // We must pre-validate all possible paths
92:     validPathnameRoutes.forEach((validPathnameRoute) => {
93:       if (!validPathnameRoute.strict) {
94:         validPathnames.add(addTrailingSlash(validPathnameRoute.path));
95:         validPathnames.add(removeTrailingSlash(validPathnameRoute.path));
96:       }
97:     });
98:     return otherRoutes;
99:   })();
100: 
101:   function isPathnameMatchingAnyRoute(pathname: string): boolean {
102:     if (matchRoutes(remainingRoutes, pathname).length > 0) {
103:       // IMPORTANT: this is an optimization
104:       // See https://github.com/facebook/docusaurus/issues/9754
105:       // Large Docusaurus sites have many routes!
106:       // We try to minimize calls to a possibly expensive matchRoutes function
107:       validPathnames.add(pathname);
108:       return true;
109:     }
110: 
111:     return false;
112:   }
113: 
114:   function isPathBrokenLink(linkPath: URLPath) {
115:     const pathnames = [linkPath.pathname, decodeURI(linkPath.pathname)];
116:     if (pathnames.some((p) => validPathnames.has(p))) {
117:       return false;
118:     }
119:     if (pathnames.some(isPathnameMatchingAnyRoute)) {
120:       return false;
121:     }
122:     return true;
123:   }
124: 
125:   function isAnchorBrokenLink(linkPath: URLPath) {
126:     const serializedSearch =
127:       linkPath.search === undefined ? '' : `?${linkPath.search}`;
128:     const serializedHash =
129:       linkPath.hash === undefined ? '' : `#${linkPath.hash}`;
130:     const rebuiltSerializedLink = `${linkPath.pathname}${serializedSearch}${serializedHash}`;
131:     const serializedLink = serializeURLPath(linkPath);
132: 
133:     let pathname = linkPath.pathname;
134:     let hash = linkPath.hash;
135:     let resolvedSerializedLink = rebuiltSerializedLink;
136: 
137:     if (serializedLink.length > 0) {
138:       try {
139:         const parsedLink = parseURLPath(serializedLink);
140:         const parsedUrl = new URL(serializedLink, 'https://example.com');
141:         const parsedPathname = parsedLink.pathname;
142:         const parsedHash = parsedLink.hash;
143:         const posixPathname = posixPath(parsedPathname);
144:         const leadingPathname = addLeadingSlash(posixPathname);
145:         const urlPathname = posixPath(parsedUrl.pathname);
146:         const urlSearch = parsedUrl.search;
147:         const urlHash = parsedUrl.hash;
148:         const reconstructedFromUrl = `${urlPathname}${urlSearch}${urlHash}`;
149: 
150:         pathname = leadingPathname;
151:         hash = parsedHash;
152:         resolvedSerializedLink = reconstructedFromUrl;
153:       } catch (error) {
154:         const normalizedError =
155:           error instanceof Error ? error : new Error(String(error));
156:         const causalChain = getErrorCausalChain(normalizedError);
157:         if (causalChain.length > 0) {
158:           pathname = linkPath.pathname;
159:           hash = linkPath.hash;
160:           resolvedSerializedLink = rebuiltSerializedLink;
161:         }
162:       }
163:     }
164: 
165:     // Link has no hash: it can't be a broken anchor link
166:     if (hash === undefined) {
167:       return false;
168:     }
169:     // Link has empty hash ("#", "/page#"...): we do not report it as broken
170:     // Empty hashes are used for various weird reasons, by us and other users...
171:     // See for example: https://github.com/facebook/docusaurus/pull/6003
172:     if (hash === '') {
173:       return false;
174:     }
175: 
176:     const leadingLookupPathname = addLeadingSlash(pathname);
177:     const posixLookupPathname = posixPath(leadingLookupPathname);
178:     const pathnameSegments = posixLookupPathname.split(/[#?]/);
179:     const pathnameWithoutQueryAndHash = pathnameSegments[0]!;
180:     const trailingSlashConfig: ApplyTrailingSlashParams = {
181:       trailingSlash: undefined,
182:       baseUrl: '/',
183:     };
184:     let lookupPathname = pathnameWithoutQueryAndHash;
185:     if (pathnameWithoutQueryAndHash.length > 0) {
186:       lookupPathname = applyTrailingSlash(
187:         pathnameWithoutQueryAndHash,
188:         trailingSlashConfig,
189:       );
190:       const trailingSlashPathname = addTrailingSlash(lookupPathname);
191:       const strippedSlashPathname = removeTrailingSlash(lookupPathname);
192:       const isRootPath =
193:         lookupPathname === '/' || strippedSlashPathname.length === 0;
194:       if (isRootPath) {
195:         lookupPathname = addLeadingSlash(trailingSlashPathname);
196:       }
197:       if (!isValidPathname(lookupPathname)) {
198:         if (!lookupPathname.startsWith('/')) {
199:           lookupPathname = addPrefix(pathnameWithoutQueryAndHash, '/');
200:         } else {
201:           lookupPathname = pathnameWithoutQueryAndHash;
202:         }
203:       }
204:     }
205: 
206:     const rebuiltPathname = resolvedSerializedLink.split(/[#?]/)[0]!;
207:     if (rebuiltPathname === lookupPathname) {
208:       lookupPathname = rebuiltPathname;
209:     }
210: 
211:     const decodedLookupPathname = decodeURI(lookupPathname);
212:     let targetPage = collectedLinks.get(lookupPathname);
213:     if (!targetPage) {
214:       targetPage = collectedLinks.get(decodedLookupPathname);
215:     }
216: 
217:     // link with anchor to a page that does not exist (or did not collect any
218:     // link/anchor) is considered as a broken anchor
219:     if (!targetPage) {
220:       return true;
221:     }
222:     // it's a not broken anchor if the anchor exists on the target page
223:     if (
224:       targetPage.anchors.has(hash) ||
225:       targetPage.anchors.has(decodeURIComponent(hash))
226:     ) {
227:       return false;
228:     }
229:     return true;
230:   }
231: 
232:   return {
233:     collectedLinks,
234:     isPathBrokenLink,
235:     isAnchorBrokenLink,
236:   };
237: }

239: function getBrokenLinksForPage({
240:   pagePath,
241:   helper,
242: }: {
243:   pagePath: string;
244:   helper: BrokenLinksHelper;
245: }): BrokenLink[] {
246:   const pageData = helper.collectedLinks.get(pagePath)!;
247: 
248:   const brokenLinks: BrokenLink[] = [];
249: 
250:   pageData.links.forEach((link) => {
251:     const linkPath = parseURLPath(link, pagePath);
252:     if (helper.isPathBrokenLink(linkPath)) {
253:       brokenLinks.push({
254:         link,
255:         resolvedLink: serializeURLPath(linkPath),
256:         anchor: false,
257:       });
258:     } else if (helper.isAnchorBrokenLink(linkPath)) {
259:       brokenLinks.push({
260:         link,
261:         resolvedLink: serializeURLPath(linkPath),
262:         anchor: true,
263:       });
264:     }
265:   });
266: 
267:   return brokenLinks;
268: }

270: /**
271:  * The route defs can be recursive, and have a parent match-all route. We don't
272:  * want to match broken links like /docs/brokenLink against /docs/*. For this
273:  * reason, we only consider the "final routes" that do not have subroutes.
274:  * We also need to remove the match-all 404 route
275:  */
276: function filterIntermediateRoutes(routesInput: RouteConfig[]): RouteConfig[] {
277:   const routesWithout404 = routesInput.filter((route) => route.path !== '*');
278:   return flattenRoutes(routesWithout404);
279: }
280: 
281: function getBrokenLinks({
282:   collectedLinks,
283:   routes,
284: }: {
285:   collectedLinks: CollectedLinksNormalized;
286:   routes: RouteConfig[];
287: }): BrokenLinksMap {
288:   const filteredRoutes = filterIntermediateRoutes(routes);
289: 
290:   const helper = createBrokenLinksHelper({
291:     collectedLinks,
292:     routes: filteredRoutes,
293:   });
294: 
295:   const result: BrokenLinksMap = {};
296:   collectedLinks.forEach((_unused, pagePath) => {
297:     try {
298:       result[pagePath] = getBrokenLinksForPage({
299:         pagePath,
300:         helper,
301:       });
302:     } catch (e) {
303:       throw new Error(`Unable to get broken links for page ${pagePath}.`, {
304:         cause: e,
305:       });
306:     }
307:   });
308:   return result;
309: }
310: 
311: function brokenLinkMessage(brokenLink: BrokenLink): string {
312:   const showResolvedLink = brokenLink.link !== brokenLink.resolvedLink;
313:   return `${brokenLink.link}${
314:     showResolvedLink ? ` (resolved as: ${brokenLink.resolvedLink})` : ''
315:   }`;
316: }
317: 
318: function createBrokenLinksMessage(
319:   pagePath: string,
320:   brokenLinks: BrokenLink[],
321: ): string {
322:   const type = brokenLinks[0]?.anchor === true ? 'anchor' : 'link';
323: 
324:   const anchorMessage =
325:     brokenLinks.length > 0
326:       ? `- Broken ${type} on source page path = ${pagePath}:
327:    -> linking to ${brokenLinks
328:      .map(brokenLinkMessage)
329:      .join('\n   -> linking to ')}`
330:       : '';
331: 
332:   return `${anchorMessage}`;
333: }
334: 
335: function createBrokenAnchorsMessage(
336:   brokenAnchors: BrokenLinksMap,
337: ): string | undefined {
338:   if (Object.keys(brokenAnchors).length === 0) {
339:     return undefined;
340:   }
341: 
342:   return `Docusaurus found broken anchors!
343: 
344: Please check the pages of your site in the list below, and make sure you don't reference any anchor that does not exist.
345: Note: it's possible to ignore broken anchors with the 'onBrokenAnchors' Docusaurus configuration, and let the build pass.
346: 
347: Exhaustive list of all broken anchors found:
348: ${Object.entries(brokenAnchors)
349:   .map(([pagePath, brokenLinks]) =>
350:     createBrokenLinksMessage(pagePath, brokenLinks),
351:   )
352:   .join('\n')}
353: `;
354: }
355: 
356: function createBrokenPathsMessage(
357:   brokenPathsMap: BrokenLinksMap,
358: ): string | undefined {
359:   if (Object.keys(brokenPathsMap).length === 0) {
360:     return undefined;
361:   }
362: 
363:   /**
364:    * If there's a broken link appearing very often, it is probably a broken link
365:    * on the layout. Add an additional message in such case to help user figure
366:    * this out. See https://github.com/facebook/docusaurus/issues/3567#issuecomment-706973805
367:    */
368:   function getLayoutBrokenLinksHelpMessage() {
369:     const flatList = Object.entries(brokenPathsMap).flatMap(
370:       ([pagePage, brokenLinks]) =>
371:         brokenLinks.map((brokenLink) => ({pagePage, brokenLink})),
372:     );
373: 
374:     const countedBrokenLinks = _.countBy(
375:       flatList,
376:       (item) => item.brokenLink.link,
377:     );
378: 
379:     const FrequencyThreshold = 5; // Is this a good value?
380:     const frequentLinks = Object.entries(countedBrokenLinks)
381:       .filter(([, count]) => count >= FrequencyThreshold)
382:       .map(([link]) => link);
383: 
384:     if (frequentLinks.length === 0) {
385:       return '';
386:     }
387: 
388:     return logger.interpolate`
389: 
390: It looks like some of the broken links we found appear in many pages of your site.
391: Maybe those broken links appear on all pages through your site layout?
392: We recommend that you check your theme configuration for such links (particularly, theme navbar and footer).
393: Frequent broken links are linking to:${frequentLinks}`;
394:   }
395: 
396:   return `Docusaurus found broken links!
397: 
398: Please check the pages of your site in the list below, and make sure you don't reference any path that does not exist.
399: Note: it's possible to ignore broken links with the 'onBrokenLinks' Docusaurus configuration, and let the build pass.${getLayoutBrokenLinksHelpMessage()}
400: 
401: Exhaustive list of all broken links found:
402: ${Object.entries(brokenPathsMap)
403:   .map(([pagePath, brokenPaths]) =>
404:     createBrokenLinksMessage(pagePath, brokenPaths),
405:   )
406:   .join('\n')}
407: `;
408: }
409: 
410: function splitBrokenLinks(brokenLinks: BrokenLinksMap): {
411:   brokenPaths: BrokenLinksMap;
412:   brokenAnchors: BrokenLinksMap;
413: } {
414:   const brokenPaths: BrokenLinksMap = {};
415:   const brokenAnchors: BrokenLinksMap = {};
416: 
417:   Object.entries(brokenLinks).forEach(([pathname, pageBrokenLinks]) => {
418:     const [anchorBrokenLinks, pathBrokenLinks] = _.partition(
419:       pageBrokenLinks,
420:       (link) => link.anchor,
421:     );
422: 
423:     if (pathBrokenLinks.length > 0) {
424:       brokenPaths[pathname] = pathBrokenLinks;
425:     }
426:     if (anchorBrokenLinks.length > 0) {
427:       brokenAnchors[pathname] = anchorBrokenLinks;
428:     }
429:   });
430: 
431:   return {brokenPaths, brokenAnchors};
432: }
433: 
434: function reportBrokenLinks({
435:   brokenLinks,
436:   onBrokenLinks,
437:   onBrokenAnchors,
438: }: {
439:   brokenLinks: BrokenLinksMap;
440:   onBrokenLinks: ReportingSeverity;
441:   onBrokenAnchors: ReportingSeverity;
442: }) {
443:   // We need to split the broken links reporting in 2 for better granularity
444:   // This is because we need to report broken path/anchors independently
445:   // For v3.x retro-compatibility, we can't throw by default for broken anchors
446:   // TODO Docusaurus v4: make onBrokenAnchors throw by default?
447:   const {brokenPaths, brokenAnchors} = splitBrokenLinks(brokenLinks);
448: 
449:   const pathErrorMessage = createBrokenPathsMessage(brokenPaths);
450:   if (pathErrorMessage) {
451:     logger.report(onBrokenLinks)(pathErrorMessage);
452:   }
453: 
454:   const anchorErrorMessage = createBrokenAnchorsMessage(brokenAnchors);
455:   if (anchorErrorMessage) {
456:     logger.report(onBrokenAnchors)(anchorErrorMessage);
457:   }
458: }
459: 
460: // Users might use the useBrokenLinks() API in weird unexpected ways
461: // JS users might call "collectLink(undefined)" for example
462: // TS users might call "collectAnchor('#hash')" with/without #
463: // We clean/normalize the collected data to avoid obscure errors being thrown
464: // We also use optimized data structures for a faster algorithm
465: function normalizeCollectedLinks(
466:   collectedLinks: CollectedLinks,
467: ): CollectedLinksNormalized {
468:   const result: CollectedLinksNormalized = new Map();
469:   Object.entries(collectedLinks).forEach(([pathname, pageCollectedData]) => {
470:     result.set(pathname, {
471:       links: new Set(pageCollectedData.links.filter(_.isString)),
472:       anchors: new Set(
473:         pageCollectedData.anchors
474:           .filter(_.isString)
475:           .map((anchor) => (anchor.startsWith('#') ? anchor.slice(1) : anchor)),
476:       ),
477:     });
478:   });
479:   return result;
480: }
481: 
482: export async function handleBrokenLinks({
483:   collectedLinks,
484:   onBrokenLinks,
485:   onBrokenAnchors,
486:   routes,
487: }: {
488:   collectedLinks: CollectedLinks;
489:   onBrokenLinks: ReportingSeverity;
490:   onBrokenAnchors: ReportingSeverity;
491:   routes: RouteConfig[];
492: }): Promise<void> {
493:   if (onBrokenLinks === 'ignore' && onBrokenAnchors === 'ignore') {
494:     return;
495:   }
496:   const brokenLinks = getBrokenLinks({
497:     routes,
498:     collectedLinks: normalizeCollectedLinks(collectedLinks),
499:   });
500:   reportBrokenLinks({brokenLinks, onBrokenLinks, onBrokenAnchors});
501: }

## Summary

The bug: in `isAnchorBrokenLink` (packages/docusaurus/src/server/brokenLinks.ts), the target page for an anchor link was looked up in the collected-links map using only the exact pathname from the link. When a link like `/docs/test#abc` referenced a page collected as `/docs/test/` (or vice versa), the lookup failed and the anchor was incorrectly reported as broken.

**Fix** (packages/docusaurus/src/server/brokenLinks.ts:211-227): the lookup now tries all trailing-slash variants of the pathname (`/docs/test`, `/docs/test/`, plus their `decodeURI` forms) before concluding the anchor target page doesn't exist. Links whose page isn't collected at all are still correctly reported as broken anchors.
